decisions.question: Which rule replaces item 4's 'lower bound is the version the committed lockfile resolves when the dependency is added', so that every member's constraints resolve at every point of the build order the phase plans allow?

options.label: lower bounds from the full planned resolution, as a table in item 4
options.consequence: Every member copies one recorded constraint per package; all 20 reachable member sets resolve from no lockfile and both orders resolve incrementally; items 1 and 7's values and the lockfile rule stay. Before nidana.flutter.1 the lockfile holds test 1.33.0 inside ^1.31.1 and moves it down there; the table must be recomputed on a pin change and a new package needs a probe.

options.label: accepted rule plus a Flutter anchor in the root
options.consequence: flutter_test as a root dev dependency from nidana.model.1 makes the accepted rule write the table's constraints and resolve at every stage of both orders tried, with no test move at nidana.flutter.1; it changes item 1 (the root gains a second dependency) and item 4's 'Flutter appears only in' bullet, and each constraint still depends on which members exist when it is written.

options.label: accepted rule unchanged
options.consequence: nidana.model.1 writes test: ^1.33.0 and package_config: ^3.0.0; nidana.flutter.1's pub get fails along both orders.

options.label: lowest working version checked by pub downgrade
options.consequence: Honest bounds for publication, but every member-creating phase runs a downgrade resolution that nothing else in the tree uses.

decisions.chosen: lower bounds from the full planned resolution, as a table in item 4
decisions.why: It is the only option that meets the brief's whole requirement: the experiment shows every reachable member set resolves (P4, 20 of 20) and both orders resolve incrementally with --enforce-lockfile passing after every stage and a final lockfile equal to a fresh full resolution (P5a, P5b, P6), while item 1's root, the lockfile rule and item 7's pin values stay as written. The anchor also resolves (P3a, P3b) and avoids the test move at nidana.flutter.1, but it changes items 1 and 4 and leaves constraints order-dependent. The accepted rule fails on two packages, not one: package_config ^3.0.0 fails beside a Flutter member on its own (P2c). Close call between the table and the anchor; the signal that would have changed my mind is a member test that needs a test API newer than 1.31.1 before nidana.flutter.1, or a second direct package held above its lower bound before the first Flutter member (P4 shows test is the only one today).

decisions.question: Context Q11c records exit 3 for a plugin that does not compile, and plugin-rebuild R6 observed exit 4. Which fact does the ADR state?

options.label: state the general rule
options.consequence: Diagnostics decide the exit (3 ERROR, 2 WARNING, INFO 0 or 1 under --fatal-infos); 4 only when nothing analyzed reports; the root analyze reports the plugin's own broken source as an ERROR, so exit 3 there; plain analyze with only INFOs exits 0 with the plugin not loaded.

options.label: replace 3 with 4
options.consequence: Wrong for the root analyze, which the gates run: E1 reproduces Q11c's exit 3.

decisions.why: plugin-compile-exit shows both observations were right for their shapes: Q11c ran the root analyze, whose ERROR on the plugin's broken source it filtered from its output (exit 3, E1); R6 analyzed a clean directory outside the plugin (exit 4, E2). E3 to E6 show the exit follows the analyzed files' diagnostics whenever there are any, so a broken plugin can exit 2, 1 or 0. The Consequences bullet keeps its claim (every root analyze under --fatal-infos fails) and now says how.

experiments.question: What exit code does fvm dart analyze give when a root-enabled plugin does not compile, and why did workspace-layout Q11c see 3 where plugin-rebuild R6 saw 4?
experiments.finding: E1: the root analyze, which also analyzes the plugin's broken source, reports that ERROR and exits 3 (Q11c's shape). E2: a clean member analyzed alone exits 4 (R6's shape). E3: WARNINGs in the analyzed files give 2; E4: an ERROR gives 3; E5: INFOs only give 0 without --fatal-infos; E6: 1 under --fatal-infos; E7: plugin restored, an ERROR gives 3. Exit 4 occurs only when nothing analyzed reports a diagnostic.
